definitionEn: to make a picture, memory or feeling appear in someone's mind
senseNote: Выбрано значение conjure (up) — вызывать образы и воспоминания; значение «показывать фокусы» не отрабатывается.
situation: A smell, word, song or place makes certain images, memories or feelings appear in your mind.

examples.text: The smell of pine trees always [[conjures]] up memories of Christmas at my grandparents' house.
The word 'Mediterranean' [[conjures]] up images of sunshine, olive trees and long lunches.
In just a few lines, the poet [[conjures]] a whole world of childhood fears.

texts: Few sounds [[conjure]] up summer better than an ice-cream van's tune.
Those old photos [[conjure]] up the whole atmosphere of the 1970s.
Good travel writers can [[conjure]] up a place in just a few sentences.

badCollocation.noteRu: Интерес вызывают — arouse или spark interest. Conjure up — вызывать образы и воспоминания, картинки в голове.

collocationTask.prompt: The name alone ___ up images of luxury.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Вызывать образы в голове — conjure up images. Raise, lift и put up значат «поднимать» или «вешать», про воображение так не говорят.

nuance.text: Her paintings [[conjure]] a world of quiet villages and empty beaches.
nuance.explanationRu: Conjure (up) — вызывать образы и картинки в воображении. Invoke — ссылаться на закон или правило, призывать: invoke a rule.

reverse.text: The company [[invoked]] a clause in the contract to cancel the deal.
reverse.explanationRu: Сослаться на пункт договора — invoke a clause. Conjure — про образы и воспоминания.

fixIt.text: The old song [[woke]] up memories of my first year at university.
fixIt.explanationRu: Wake up — просыпаться или будить человека. Вызвать воспоминания — conjure up memories.

definitionEn: to succeed in overcoming a fear, weakness or difficult problem through effort
senseNote: Выбрано значение «побороть, преодолеть» (conquer your fear); военное «завоевать» — базовое значение и не отрабатывается.
situation: After a long struggle, you finally beat a fear, bad habit, illness or personal weakness.

examples.text: After months of lessons, she finally [[conquered]] her fear of deep water.
Scientists hope the new vaccine will help [[conquer]] a disease that kills thousands every year.
It took me months to [[conquer]] my habit of checking emails every five minutes.

texts: Exposure therapy can help people [[conquer]] a fear of spiders.
You'll never [[conquer]] your nerves if you keep avoiding public speaking.
Few of us ever completely [[conquer]] our shyness.

badCollocation.noteRu: Соревнование или конкурс выигрывают — win a competition. Conquer — побороть страх, болезнь, слабость.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Побороть страх — conquer (или overcome, beat) your fear. Defend — защищать, gain и earn — получать или зарабатывать.

nuance.text: He finally [[conquered]] his shyness and asked her out.
nuance.explanationRu: Conquer — побороть чувство или слабость: вы сильнее. Overwhelm — наоборот, чувство «накрывает» вас: she was overwhelmed by fear.

reverse.text: On her first day at the new school, she was [[overwhelmed]] by the noise and the crowds.
reverse.explanationRu: Когда впечатления захлёстывают, говорят be overwhelmed by. Conquer — самому побороть что-то.

fixIt.text: She has finally [[won]] her fear of driving on motorways.
fixIt.explanationRu: Win — выиграть матч или приз. Страх побеждают по-другому: conquer (или overcome) your fear.

wordFormation.text: The [[conquest]] of polio is one of the great success stories of modern medicine.

reply.context: A friend says: "I finally gave a talk to two hundred people, and my voice didn't even shake!"
options: That's huge! You've really conquered your fear of public speaking.
That's huge! Now you can conquer a medal for it.
Your conquest of stage fright is duly acknowledged and commended.
reply.explanationRu: Conquer your fear — побороть страх, первый ответ естественный. Во втором conquer ошибочно значит «завоевать награду», третий звучит как официальная грамота.

rewrite.original: It took him years to get over his fear of dogs.
rewrite.frame: It took him years to ____ of dogs.

definitionEn: the part of your mind that tells you whether your actions are right or wrong
situation: You feel guilty after doing something wrong, or an inner voice stops you from doing it.

examples.text: He couldn't keep the money he found; his [[conscience]] wouldn't let him.
I can't sign off these figures with a clear [[conscience]]: they're simply not accurate.
Several politicians voted against the law as a matter of [[conscience]].

texts: Your [[conscience]] is telling you to apologise, isn't it?
She lost her job for refusing to act against her [[conscience]].
The charity appeals to the [[conscience]] of wealthy donors.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Совесть мучает» — my conscience is bothering me или I have a guilty conscience; tortures звучит неестественно.

collocationTask.prompt: I have a guilty ___ about missing her party.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Нечистая совесть — a guilty conscience. Conscious — прилагательное «в сознании», consensus — общее согласие, concern — беспокойство.

nuance.text: When you're not sure what to do, let your [[conscience]] be your guide.
nuance.explanationRu: Conscience — совесть, внутренний голос, который подсказывает, что правильно. Guilt — само чувство вины; оно не может быть «проводником».

reverse.text: She felt a lot of [[guilt]] about missing her son's school play.
reverse.explanationRu: Чувство вины испытывают — feel guilt. Conscience — совесть, её не «чувствуют много».

fixIt.text: Cheating in the exam would be against my [[consciousness]], so I won't do it.
fixIt.explanationRu: Consciousness — сознание (lose consciousness). Против совести — against my conscience.

wordFormation.text: Nurses on the night shift have to be especially [[conscientious]] about checking medication.

reply.context: A friend says: "The cashier gave me ten euros too much change. Should I just keep it?"
options: One's conscience would presumably dictate the restitution of said funds.
Sure, just lose conscience for a minute and nobody will notice.
Could you really keep it with a clear conscience? I'd give it back.
reply.explanationRu: With a clear conscience — с чистой совестью, третий ответ естественный. Во втором conscience спутано с consciousness («потерять сознание»), первый звучит как старинный трактат.

definitionEn: careful to do your work or duties thoroughly, correctly and on time
situation: You describe a student or employee who always checks details, meets deadlines and never cuts corners.

examples.text: She is a [[conscientious]] employee who always checks her work twice before sending it.
The most [[conscientious]] students had started revising weeks before the exam.
Being a [[conscientious]] tenant, he reported the leak to the landlord immediately.

texts: He's so [[conscientious]] that he answers work emails on holiday.
A [[conscientious]] doctor will always explain the risks of a treatment.
Thanks to a few [[conscientious]] volunteers, the park is always clean.

badCollocation.noteRu: Невольная ошибка — an honest mistake. Conscientious описывает старательного человека или тщательную работу.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Добросовестная в работе — conscientious about her work. Consistent — последовательный, considerate — внимательный к другим, continuous — непрерывный.

nuance.text: Tom is the most [[conscientious]] member of the team: he never misses a deadline.
nuance.explanationRu: Conscientious — добросовестный, старательный. Conscious — осознающий что-то или находящийся в сознании: conscious of the risks. Слова похожи, но значат разное.

reverse.text: Are you [[conscious]] of how loudly you're talking?
reverse.explanationRu: Осознавать что-то — be conscious of something. Conscientious — добросовестный, к осознанию отношения не имеет.

fixIt.text: Our new assistant is very [[executive]]: she does everything on time and checks every detail.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «исполнительный» — не executive (это «руководитель»), а conscientious или reliable.

wordFormation.text: Employers often value [[conscientiousness]] more than raw talent.

reply.context: Your manager asks: "Who should we put in charge of checking the contracts?"
options: Anna. She's the most conscientious person on the team and never misses a detail.
Anna. She's very conscientious, so she'll probably skip the boring parts.
Yo, Anna's well conscientious, trust me on that one.
reply.explanationRu: Conscientious — добросовестный, первый ответ естественный. Во втором слово понято как «небрежный», третий звучит как сленг, неуместный в разговоре с руководителем.

definitionEn: the awareness or understanding that people have of a particular issue or fact
senseNote: Выбрано значение «осознание, общественное сознание» (public consciousness); базовое «сознание» (lose consciousness, B2) не отрабатывается.
situation: You talk about how aware a society or group is of an issue such as pollution or inequality.

examples.text: Over the last decade, climate change has firmly entered the public [[consciousness]].
The strikes of the 1970s created a new political [[consciousness]] among young workers.
Growing [[consciousness]] of the risks of sugar has changed the way people shop.

texts: Recycling only became part of the national [[consciousness]] in the 1990s.
The campaign aims to raise [[consciousness]] about mental health at work.
Her novels reflect the growing environmental [[consciousness]] of her generation.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Прийти к осознанию» — come to the realisation that. Consciousness — осознание проблемы обществом или группой.

collocationTask.prompt: The film did a lot to ___ consciousness of homelessness.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Повышать осознание проблемы — raise consciousness (или awareness). Rise и arise непереходные, а grow с таким дополнением не сочетается.

nuance.text: The novel explores how a working-class [[consciousness]] developed in industrial cities.
nuance.explanationRu: Consciousness — осознание группой своего положения и интересов (class consciousness). Conscience — совесть, чувство правильного и неправильного.

reverse.text: My [[conscience]] tells me I should return the wallet.
reverse.explanationRu: Внутренний голос, совесть — conscience. Consciousness — сознание или осознание, а не мораль.

fixIt.text: Environmental [[conscious]] among teenagers has grown enormously in recent years.
fixIt.explanationRu: Conscious — прилагательное. Нужно существительное: environmental consciousness — экологическое сознание.

wordFormation.text: There is a growing [[consciousness]] among shoppers that cheap clothes have hidden costs.

definitionEn: following one after another in a series, without any break
situation: The same thing happens several times in a row, with no break between the days, games or years.

examples.text: The team has now won five [[consecutive]] matches without conceding a goal.
It has rained for twelve [[consecutive]] days, and the river is close to flooding.
This is the third [[consecutive]] year that the company has cut its training budget.

texts: She was elected for a second [[consecutive]] term.
The temperature stayed above forty degrees for three [[consecutive]] days.
He missed four [[consecutive]] classes and was asked to see the head teacher.

badCollocation.noteRu: Связный, логичный рассказ — a coherent story. Consecutive — идущие подряд по времени или счёту.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Третий год подряд — the third consecutive year (или successive). Consistent — стабильный, consequent — вытекающий из чего-то, continual — постоянно повторяющийся.

nuance.text: He scored in six [[consecutive]] games before getting injured.
nuance.explanationRu: Consecutive — идущие подряд, без перерыва. Consistent — стабильный по качеству или взглядам. Оба переводятся «последовательный», но значат разное.

reverse.text: Her results have been [[consistent]] all year: never below ninety per cent.
reverse.explanationRu: Стабильные результаты — consistent. Consecutive говорит только о порядке «подряд», а не о качестве.

fixIt.text: It snowed for five [[subsequent]] days, so the schools stayed closed.
fixIt.explanationRu: Subsequent — последующий, случившийся позже. Пять дней подряд — five consecutive days.

wordFormation.text: The pages are numbered [[consecutively]] from one to two hundred.

rewrite.original: She won the championship in 2022, 2023 and 2024.
rewrite.frame: She won the championship for three ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Three consecutive years — три года подряд.

definitionEn: general agreement among all or most of the people in a group
situation: After discussion, nearly everyone in a group, meeting or field of study agrees on something.

examples.text: After three hours of discussion, the committee finally reached a [[consensus]] on the budget.
There is a broad scientific [[consensus]] that regular exercise lowers the risk of heart disease.
The government wants to build a national [[consensus]] before changing the pension system.

texts: There is no [[consensus]] among experts about the best diet.
The decision was made by [[consensus]], not by a vote.
A [[consensus]] is slowly emerging that the old building should be saved.

badCollocation.noteRu: Консенсуса достигают — reach (или come to) a consensus; make здесь не подходит.

collocationTask.prompt: There is a broad ___ among doctors that sleep matters.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Общее мнение специалистов — a broad consensus. Census — перепись населения, concession — уступка, consistency — постоянство.

nuance.text: Everyone liked the plan from the start, so reaching a [[consensus]] was easy.
nuance.explanationRu: Consensus — все согласны с одним решением. Compromise — каждая сторона чем-то жертвует, чтобы договориться; здесь спорить было не о чем.

reverse.text: Neither side got everything it wanted, so the final deal was a [[compromise]].
reverse.explanationRu: Когда обе стороны уступают, получается compromise. Consensus — единое мнение без взаимных уступок.

fixIt.text: The ministers failed to reach a [[consent]] on the new rules.
fixIt.explanationRu: Consent — разрешение, согласие на что-то. Общее мнение группы — consensus: reach a consensus.

reply.context: In a team meeting, your manager says: "So, does everyone agree we should move the launch to May?"
options: I think we have a consensus. Nobody has raised any objections.
I think we have a consensus, although half the team is still against it.
Consensus achieved, boss! High fives all round, yeah?
reply.explanationRu: Consensus — общее согласие, первый ответ естественный. Во втором консенсус противоречит тому, что половина команды против, третий слишком фамильярный для совещания.

rewrite.original: Most economists agree that the tax will not work.
rewrite.frame: There is a broad ____ that the tax will not work.
rewrite.explanationRu: A broad consensus among — общее мнение большинства.

definitionEn: permission for something to happen, or agreement to do something
situation: A doctor, company or school needs a person's formal permission before doing something that affects them.

examples.text: Doctors must get the patient's [[consent]] before carrying out any operation.
The app shared users' personal data without their [[consent]].
Students under eighteen need written [[consent]] from a parent to go on the trip.

texts: Silence should never be taken as [[consent]].
They separated by mutual [[consent]] after ten years together.
Parental [[consent]] is required for children under thirteen.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Жить в согласии» — live in harmony. Consent — формальное разрешение на что-то.

collocationTask.prompt: The patient must ___ written consent before the operation.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Дать согласие — give (или provide) consent. Make, do и say с consent не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The surgeon explained the risks and then asked for the patient's [[consent]].
nuance.explanationRu: Consent — разрешение одного человека на то, что касается его самого. Consensus — общее мнение группы; у одного пациента консенсуса не бывает.

reverse.text: After a long debate, the group reached a [[consensus]] on the new schedule.
reverse.explanationRu: Единое мнение группы — consensus. Consent — разрешение, его дают, а не «достигают».

fixIt.text: The magazine printed the photos without the actor's [[acceptance]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Acceptance — принятие (идеи, приглашения). Разрешение человека на публикацию — consent.

reply.context: A new colleague asks: "Can I add everyone's phone numbers to the team group chat?"
options: Sure, give them your consent and they'll join automatically.
Only with their consent. Some people prefer to keep their number private.
Consent must be procured from each and every individual concerned forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: With their consent — с их согласия, второй ответ естественный. В первом перепутано, кто даёт согласие, третий звучит как юридический приказ.

rewrite.original: Nobody asked me whether I agreed to the changes.
rewrite.explanationRu: Without my consent — без моего согласия.

definitionEn: to use as little of something as possible so that it lasts longer
senseNote: Выбрано значение «экономить, беречь ресурс» (conserve energy, water); значение «охранять природу и памятники» не отрабатывается.
situation: You try to use less water, energy or strength so that there is enough left for later.

examples.text: During the drought, residents were asked to [[conserve]] water by taking shorter showers.
The runner [[conserved]] her energy for the final lap and then overtook everyone.
To [[conserve]] battery power, the phone automatically dims the screen after thirty seconds.

texts: Turn off the lights when you leave to [[conserve]] electricity.
Camels can [[conserve]] water for days in the desert.
Patients should [[conserve]] their strength for the first few days after surgery.

badCollocation.noteRu: Деньги копят или экономят — save money. Conserve — экономно расходовать ресурсы: воду, энергию, силы.

collocationTask.prompt: Please turn off the heating to ___ energy.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Экономить энергию — conserve (или save) energy. Hold — держать, protect и guard — охранять от опасности; «беречь энергию» так не переводится.

nuance.text: During the heatwave, hospitals were told to [[conserve]] electricity wherever possible.
nuance.explanationRu: Conserve — расходовать экономно, чтобы хватило: электричество, воду, силы. Preserve — сохранить в неизменном виде (традиции, здания) или заготовить еду.

reverse.text: My grandmother [[preserves]] plums in sugar every autumn.
reverse.explanationRu: Заготовить фрукты на зиму — preserve (или make jam). Conserve — экономить ресурсы, а не консервировать.

fixIt.text: Experienced hikers [[keep]] their energy by walking slowly at the start of the day.
fixIt.explanationRu: Keep energy так не говорят. Расходовать силы экономно — conserve energy.

wordFormation.text: Simple habits like switching off lights make a real difference to energy [[conservation]].

reply.context: Your flatmate asks: "Why do you always switch the heating off when you leave the room?"
options: Just trying to conserve energy. Our bills are huge.
Just trying to conserve the room, so it stays exactly as it is.
I am endeavouring to conserve thermal resources in accordance with best practice.
reply.explanationRu: Conserve energy — экономить энергию, первый ответ естественный. Во втором conserve ошибочно значит «сохранить в неизменном виде», третий звучит как отчёт, а не ответ соседу.

definitionEn: the quality of always behaving, performing or being the same over time
senseNote: Выбрано значение «постоянство, стабильность» (consistency in quality); значение «консистенция, густота» не отрабатывается.
situation: Someone keeps the same quality, behaviour or opinions over time, without sudden ups and downs.

examples.text: What makes her a great player is her [[consistency]]: she rarely has a bad game.
Customers expect [[consistency]], so every branch uses exactly the same recipes.
Critics pointed out a lack of [[consistency]]: the minister said one thing in March and the opposite in May.

texts: Good parenting requires [[consistency]], not perfection.
The key to learning a language is [[consistency]]: a little every day.
Fans have been impressed by the [[consistency]] of the team's results this season.

badCollocation.noteRu: Порядок, последовательность событий — the sequence of events. Consistency — постоянство, стабильность.

collocationTask.prompt: Customers value ___ in quality above everything else.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Стабильное качество — consistency in quality. Consequence — последствие, coincidence — совпадение, consensus — общее согласие.

nuance.text: Her [[consistency]] is remarkable: she has scored between 85 and 90 in every test this year.
nuance.explanationRu: Consistency — стабильно одинаковый результат. Persistence — упорство, когда продолжаешь несмотря на трудности; ровные оценки — это стабильность.

reverse.text: It took real [[persistence]] to get the council to fix the road after two years of complaints.
reverse.explanationRu: Добиться своего после двух лет жалоб — это упорство, persistence. Consistency — постоянство уровня или поведения.

fixIt.text: The best thing about this café is the [[stability]] of its coffee: it's good every single time.
fixIt.explanationRu: Stability — устойчивость (экономики, конструкции). Одинаково хорошее качество каждый раз — consistency.

wordFormation.text: Athletes who train with [[consistency]] improve faster than those who train hard only occasionally.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How did you get so good at the guitar in just a year?"
options: The key determinant of my progress was, in essence, a consistency of praxis.
Consistency, really. The strings are thick and a bit sticky.
Consistency, really. I practised for twenty minutes every single day.
reply.explanationRu: Consistency — регулярность и постоянство, третий ответ естественный. Во втором слово понято как «консистенция, густота», первый звучит как научная статья.
